decks.name: Small Town Campaign Start
decks.description: A grounded beginning for a party that starts life in a quiet frontier town. Most of the cards go into the bonds between the characters and the texture of the place they call home, then a few institutions, rivalries, and half-buried secrets are salted in. By the end you should have a town that feels lived-in, a web of relationships the players actually care about, and two or three loose threads the GM can pull on whenever the campaign needs a direction.
focus: Define what makes the town unique.
Leave two or three adventure hooks.

decks.name: New Player Joins the Party
decks.description: A short deck for folding a new character into an established group without an awkward 'you all meet at a tavern' restart. It leans hard on relationships and shared memory so the newcomer arrives already tangled in the party's history, then leaves a single unresolved question hanging over them. Run it in the session a new player joins.
focus: Give the new character existing connections.
Create at least one shared memory.
Give the party a reason to trust (or question) them.
Leave one unresolved mystery involving the newcomer.

decks.name: Political Intrigue
decks.description: A campaign of nobles, guilds, and shifting alliances where the sharpest weapon is information. The deck front-loads political tensions and the organizations that embody them, gives those factions faces the players know personally, and deliberately avoids clean sides. Expect competing interests, useful enemies, and allies who may not stay allies.

decks.name: Merchant Guild Campaign
decks.description: For a party whose fortunes rise and fall with commerce, exploration, and trade. The deck emphasizes the economy, the guilds and companies that move goods, and the opportunities worth chasing, with a thread of travel and politics to keep the money entangled with the world. You should come away with valuable goods, contested trade routes, influential merchants, and rivals who want what you have.
focus: Define valuable goods and trade routes.

decks.name: Frontier Exploration
decks.description: A newly settled region where the map still has blank spaces and every landmark hides a story. The deck weights wilderness, the opportunities a frontier offers, and the fragile communities clinging to it, threaded with travel and the deep history buried underfoot. Use it to define landmarks, mark out the dangerous places, and seed the ancient ruins the party will eventually be foolish enough to enter.
focus: Seed ancient ruins and forgotten history.

decks.name: Kingdom at War
decks.description: The campaign opens with two nations already at each other's throats and the party caught in the middle. The deck spends its weight on conflict, the politics driving it, and the history that made it inevitable, while keeping the relationships that give the war personal stakes. It leaves room for diplomacy as much as battle, and asks why this war matters to these characters in particular.
focus: Leave room for diplomacy as well as battle.

decks.name: Mystery Campaign
decks.description: Everything here bends toward a single unknown truth. The deck is dominated by mystery and the history it's rooted in, with just enough people, factions, and politics to give the questions somewhere to live. It is built to produce conflicting theories rather than tidy answers, so the table ends up with a knot worth spending a campaign untangling.
focus: Connect mysteries to the world's past.
Create conflicting theories instead of clear answers.

decks.name: After a Year of Downtime
decks.description: For picking a campaign back up after significant in-world time has passed. The deck focuses on relationships and the community as they are now, surfacing what changed while the characters were away, then layers fresh opportunities and problems on top. Run it to reconnect the party with the people and places that matter before pushing them into whatever comes next.
focus: Introduce new opportunities and new problems.
